summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of hypertension, morbid obesity, and prior pulmonary embolism was admitted for progressive shortness of breath, cough, and low-grade fevers. She had been treated for pneumonia a month earlier, but symptoms recurred. Imaging showed worsening ground-glass opacities in the lungs and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, raising concern for sarcoidosis or infection. After negative infectious workup, she was treated for presumed bacterial pneumonia with ceftriaxone and azithromycin. Her symptoms improved, fever resolved, and oxygenation stabilized. Due to persistent exertional hypoxia, she was discharged on home oxygen. Esophageal thickening prompted initiation of pantoprazole for reflux. She will follow up in pulmonary clinic for repeat imaging and possible bronchoscopy if infiltrates persist.
